as_written: Ash clogs filters on cooling towers and settles on high‑voltage lines causing rolling blackouts within half an hour

text: Weight of ash snaps several high‑voltage power lines in Denver, knocking out service.
as_written: The weight of the ash on power lines snaps several high‑voltage cables, knocking out service to the city and its suburbs.

text: First commercial flights out of Denver International Airport are cancelled as visibility drops below minimum required for safe take‑off.
as_written: The first commercial flights out of Denver International Airport are cancelled as visibility drops below the minimum required for safe take‑off.

text: Ash front reaches the eastern seaboard by nine a.m., depositing about five millimetres of ash in New York City.
as_written: In New York City the streets are covered with a thin layer of ash, roughly five millimetres thick, enough to clog car filters and grind down brake pads.

text: Subway system in New York shuts down as ventilation fans draw ash into tunnels.
as_written: The subway system shuts down as the ventilation fans draw ash into the tunnels, and the city’s commuter rail network grinds to a halt.

text: Ash settles on the Atlantic Ocean off Virginia forming a grey slick that spreads eastward with the tide.
as_written: The ash also settles on the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Virginia, forming a grey slick that spreads eastward with the tide.

text: Grey slick reduces albedo of water surface and reflects more sunlight, cooling upper ocean layer by a fraction of a degree.
as_written: The slick reduces the albedo of the water surface and reflects more sunlight back into space, further cooling the upper ocean layer by a fraction of a degree.

text: Traffic snarls on interstate highways in the western United States as drivers abandon vehicles whose air intakes are clogged by ash.
as_written: Traffic snarls on interstate highways as drivers abandon vehicles that have sputtered out of fuel after the ash clogs air intakes.

text: Trucks carrying fresh produce from California to the Midwest are forced to stop, leading to dwindling grocery shelves in Chicago and St. Louis.
as_written: Trucks carrying fresh produce from California to the Midwest are forced to stop, leaving grocery shelves in cities like Chicago and St. Louis with dwindling stocks of lettuce, tomatoes and other perishable vegetables.

text: Ash settles on pastures in the plains, coating grass and reducing photosynthesis.
as_written: In the plains the ash settles on pastures, coating grass with a fine coat that blocks sunlight and reduces photosynthesis.

text: Cattle in Kansas begin to cough and show a drop in milk production within the first twelve hours.
as_written: Cattle in Kansas begin to cough as the ash irritates their lungs, and some herders report a noticeable drop in milk production within the first twelve hours.

text: Elk and bison in Yellowstone move to higher ground as ash thickens on valley floor, making wolves more vulnerable to debris collisions.
as_written: Wildlife in Yellowstone National Park is already affected; elk and bison are forced to move to higher ground as the ash thickens on the valley floor, and the sudden loss of visibility makes predators like wolves more vulnerable to accidental collisions with falling debris.

text: Ash cloud circles the globe once within fifteen hours, reaching the Pacific Northwest with concentrations sufficient to trigger air‑quality alerts in Seattle.
as_written: By fifteen hours the ash cloud has circled the globe once, returning to the Pacific Northwest with a concentration that is still enough to trigger the air‑quality alerts in Seattle.
source: NASA, satellite observations of volcanic ash transport

text: Global average surface temperature projected to dip by a few tenths of a degree within the next twenty‑four hours due to reduced sunlight.
as_written: The first day of the eruption has ... the cooling effect on the atmosphere is measurable, with global average surface temperature projected to dip by a few tenths of a degree within the next twenty‑four hours as the planet adjusts to the sudden loss of sunlight.

text: Surface temperature falls by three‑tenths of a degree Celsius within forty‑eight hours.

text: Cooling reaches half a degree Celsius by the end of the third day.

text: Acid rain in the Midwest drops to a pH of about four point five.

text: Early‑season corn yield forecast is reduced by roughly fifteen percent in Iowa.

text: The jet stream weakens as temperature gradient reverses, shifting storm tracks and bringing snowfall to normally rainy regions.

text: Denver emergency rooms treat about three thousand patients for respiratory irritation in the first seventy two hours.
